text:
maria: Heads-up: saw an 8-12% tail latency bump on the host path for small requests in today's perf run. Flamegraphs point at the pretokenizer + dechunk loop.
shawn: Can you drop the flamegraph link?
maria: https://perf.redwood/fg/3738 (smallwrites run). Main hot stacks: Tokenize::read_loop -> Dechunker::emit -> grpc::writev
lee: Confirmed locally. kvcache p99 also spikes when dechunk window crosses the 4KB boundary.
anita: Is this related to the mini-dechunk change from last week? It added a resequencing buffer, right?
maria: Yep — PR #4527. It reduced CPU for long streams but appears to introduce per-request allocs on short, chatty requests.
shawn: Quick profile snippet I captured:
```
# perf top
  15.2% Tokenizer::consume()
  12.7% Dechunker::emit_frag()
   9.8% grpc::Writev()
```
lee: We're doing a lot of small writev syscalls. Socket layer loses opportunity to coalesce and we fall back to more kernel crossings.
anita: Hypothesis: resequencer allocs + extra memcpy cause KV cache churn because small token keys don't stabilize long enough to be hot.
maria: Experiment idea: reuse a per-connection slab buffer and try coalescing writes within a 2ms headroom window. Also test toggling SSL_WRITEV_LIMIT and smallwrite coalescing.
shawn: Ran a microbench: enabling coalesce dropped host p99 by ~6% but increased throughput variance. Results: https://perf.redwood/runs/873
eng-bot: deploybot: canary deployed to canary-3 at 2026-03-20T09:12Z
lee: How does kernel selection fit here? If we reduce host overhead, the selector will favor larger-batch kernels, right?
maria: Exactly — the kernel selector currently uses observed token/sec and sequence-length hist. Host overhead is bleeding tokens/sec down, nudging us to small-batch kernels which are worse per-sample.
anita: Proposal: add an "ingress_efficiency" feature into kernel decisions. Simple EWMA over parse+dechunk cost per request to bias kernel choice.
shawn: +1. Also: don't switch kernels mid-session — that triggers KV cache revalidation and cold starts.
maria: I'll prototype an EWMA tag. Plan: 1) reuse slab per conn, 2) coalesce small writes within 2ms, 3) surface EWMA to kernel selector to bias towards stable kernels. Aim to canary next Tue.
lee: Rough ETA: expected net p99 delta -10% on the small-req benchmark, maybe -2% on mixed traffic.
anita: I'll draft a short RFC with benchmark numbers and the rollout plan.
maria: Drafted RFC: https://github.com/redwood/rfcs/pull/189
shawn: Can we add a unit/integration test that simulates kv-hit churn? Otherwise we might regress silently.
maria: Good call — adding a synthetic kv-churn scenario to perf-tests. TODO assigned.
eng-bot: perfbot: canary metrics posted (3738492040): host-path p99 -8.1%, kv-hit-rate +0.9%
lee: Nice win. :thumbsup:
maria: Closing loop for now. Keeping this thread for follow-ups; I'll paste canary graphs and the perf histogram when available. Ping me if you hit regressions.
